newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain police break up Armed Islamic Group network.
newsitem.headline: Spain police break up Armed Islamic Group network.

text.p: Spanish police said on Wednesday they had arrested 11 suspected members of Algeria's Armed Islamic Group (GIA) operating on Spain's eastern coast.
The arrests followed several months of investigation and surveillance of "activities against state security" in the city of Valencia, police said in a statement.

The suspects were part of a network which helped smuggle members of the armed band from Algeria through Spain to the rest of Europe, providing them with false identification papers, housing and cars as well as materials to carry out crimes in other countries, police said.
All of those arrested were from Algeria and only two had entered Spain legally.

Police later raided four apartments and two warehouses, seizing vehicles, arms, mobile telephones and radio transmitters along with doctored passports from seven different countries, GIA propaganda and the clandestine Al Ansar newsletter.
About 60,000 people have been killed since January 1992 when authorities called a general election in Algeria which Islamists were set to win.

Algerian Moslem extremists have accused France of backing the military authorities in a war against them and are believed to have planted a bomb last December that killed four people in a Paris metro.
The Spanish police did not say whether those arrested had a connection to the Paris bombing.
